subject: Capacity lockstep causing unexpected request curtailment (HaloCare)
messages:

Cc: HaloCare Integration Team <integration@halocare.com>

Subject: Sudden increase in latency / 429s since morning deploy

Hi Mina / Dylan —

We started seeing a surge in p95/p99 latency this morning around 08:40 PT and a large fraction of requests are getting 429s. Traffic pattern hasn't changed from our side — the same daily batch and steady API calls from our ingestion workers. The errors started right after your announced capacity routing change (per the status note). Our production ingestion is degrading and downstream ETL jobs are queuing up.

Attached is a small sample of failing requests and a quick screenshot of our error rate. Can your team confirm whether there is an ongoing throttling change or misconfiguration on Redwood's end? This is impacting an active customer demo at 10:30.

Thanks,
Emily

Subject: Re: Sudden increase in latency / 429s since morning deploy

Emily / Mina / Dylan —

TL;DR: root cause appears to be a quota-burst interlock combined with a routing change that funneled a subset of HaloCare traffic into a capacity pool with a conservative burst token window. The pool's burst allowance was reduced during the morning rollout (intentionally) but the accompanying quota window change was not propagated to the routing policy. Net effect: requests accumulate in the token bucket, then get strict 429s when the burst allowance is consumed.

What I see so far (first-pass telemetry):
- HaloCare requests were routed to pool: rdf-pool-03 (us-west-2) starting 08:35 PT due to the new region affinity rule.
- rdf-pool-03 had a burst-window set to 15s and a burst-tokens cap at 200 tokens after the deploy at 08:30. Previously it had 60s / 800 tokens.
- Traffic pattern: many small concurrent requests from ingestion workers with little inter-request spacing — this pattern burns token-buckets quickly and results in queuing and 429s.
- p99 latency increase is partly from the queue/backpressure + retries from the client side.

Immediate mitigations I propose (can be implemented in the next 15–25 minutes):
1) Increase rdf-pool-03 burst-window back to 60s and burst-tokens to 800 (temporary revert of morning change).
2) Add a routing fallback to route HaloCare to rdf-pool-01 if rdf-pool-03 token depletion > 70% for >30s.
3) Enable lightweight request-level prefix caching for HaloCare ingestion endpoints for 10 minutes to reduce KV ops.

I can push 1) and 2) now; 3) needs a follow-up job but can be done under 40 minutes.

I'll also attach a quick request trace (attached) showing token-bucket rejections and the window mismatch.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: request-sample.json (trace snippet)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Thanks Connor — and thank you Emily for flagging this.

HaloCare team, we'll coordinate a short mitigation plan so your demo and ingestion don't fail. Proposed customer-facing steps (I can send this as an update to your platform/ops team):
- Short-term: Redwood will revert the burst-window and increase token cap for rdf-pool-03 (ops ETA: ~20 minutes).
- Mid-term: Add automated pool-fallback for HaloCare and validate routing affinity rules (ETA: today EOD).
- We will issue a credit for the unsuccessful demo time as a good-faith gesture; Mina and I will confirm amount once we know total impact.

Emily — can you confirm the start time of the demo and whether there are other HaloCare services pointing at different regions? Connor, once you confirm the revert is in place, please reply with the exact timestamp so I can update the customer.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@halocare.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note: HaloCare ingestion disrupted by quota-burst / routing interlock — immediate asks

Marissa — quick executive summary and asks (for leadership visibility and any quick decisions):

Summary: HaloCare production ingestion experienced large p99 latency and widespread 429s between ~08:40–09:30 PT after this morning's capacity/routing rollout. Root cause identified as a configuration interlock: a deliberate reduction in rdf-pool-03 burst window/tokens during the rollout but missing corresponding routing policy update to shift HaloCare traffic. The mismatch means a high-concurrency ingestion pattern exhausted the token bucket and led to strict 429 enforcement.

Customer impact: demo at 10:30 was at risk; ingestion backfill delayed; customer experienced time-limited outages and increased retry traffic. HaloCare has escalated to their leadership.

Actions taken so far:
- Connor reverted burst-window/tokens for rdf-pool-03 at 10:12 PT and enabled routing fallback. Immediate error-rate drop observed; p99 latency improved within 18 minutes.
- Dylan put together a short customer message and proposed a credit.
- Telemetry and traces collected and attached; incident record created: https://redwood.app/ops/incidents/HC-3472

Asks for execs (please advise):
1) Approve a goodwill credit for HaloCare for the affected window (recommendation: 1 week of usage credit applied pro-rata; Dylan to confirm specific delta).
2) Approve an immediate pause on further capacity/routing rollouts for pools with customer-facing affinity rules until we complete a policy gating checklist (ops/infra will draft).
3) If leadership agrees, schedule a brief post-mortem with HaloCare (today or tomorrow) to review changes and agree on rollout guardrails.

I'll prepare a short post-mortem and rollout checklist; Connor and infra will supply the config diffs.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
